Alex — thanks, this is helpful. Attached are two artifacts to start: token-econ-hypotheses.xlsx (hypotheses + baseline unit-econ) and prefetch-sim-results.csv (simple sim for your profile). I sketched a short MAP gating checklist below — this is intentionally actionable so procurement can sign off on the pilot.

MAP gating checklist (initial):
- Traffic profile confirmation: steady QPS / peak QPS / request token distribution (you gave a great start; if you can share sample payloads that helps).
- Baseline tokens/request: prompt tokens + expected generation tokens (we'll use both median and P90 for pricing scenarios).
- Batching strategy: recommend starting with adaptive batching target 3–6 across non-latency-critical calls; measure latency impact at 95th percentile.
- Caching eligibility: mark static patient context (demographics, prior notes) suitable for KV-prefix caching; cache hit expected to reduce prompt tokens by ~25–55% depending on overlap.
- Unit-econ gates: baseline tokens/$ and required tokens/$ to meet your procurement target (we need your target $/1000 tokens or overall per-session budget).
- Acceptance tests: 1) End-to-end sample set (50 patient examples) — output quality parity; 2) Throughput test at 1.5x expected peak for 15 minutes; 3) Regression on latency with batching/caching enabled.
- Fallbacks: staged model variant fallbacks (smaller quantized model) with documented quality degradation.

Back-of-envelope numbers (very rough, pre-quantization):
- Assume model throughput cost equivalence of ~0.0009 $/token for full-precision large model (this is a placeholder; we'll tighten).
- If average total tokens/request = prompt 1,200 + generation 350 = 1,550 tokens -> ~1,550 * 0.0009 = $1.40 / request.
- With 40% effective prefix caching and 4x batching efficiency on token compute, an operational tokens/$ improvement can bring per-request to ~ $0.10–0.40 (highly workload dependent).

Next asks: can you confirm the procurement target (tokens/$ or $/session) and share a small sample of 10 anonymized payloads so we can run the hypothesis workbook? I’ll loop Ben and Karthik for a quick sanity-sweep of the sim assumptions.

Quick sanity notes — rough, but grounded in our recent prefetched + quantized evals: 

Assumptions (Slate profile):
- Prompt tokens (median): 1,100; prompt tokens (P90): 1,850.
- Generation: median 320, P90 520.
- Baseline total tokens/request (median): ~1,420.

Compute/econ assumptions (example model family we discussed):
- Baseline raw cost: 0.00095 $/token (full-precision LLM variant).
- Prefetch/prefix caching: realistic hit rate 30–45% for repeated context across visits; hit rate depends on how much of the prompt can be prefetched and kept in KV cache. Cache reduction applied to prompt tokens only.
- Batching: effective speedup on GPU utilization ~2.8x at batch=4, ~4.8x at batch=8 for longer sequences; latency tradeoffs vary — for your P95 target we recommend keeping interactive flows at batching <=4.

Illustrative scenarios (rounded):
1) No caching, minimal batching (batch=1): 1,420 * 0.00095 ≈ $1.35/request.
2) 35% cache on prompt + batch=4 efficiency (compute scaling 2.8x): effective compute tokens ≈ (prompt*(1-0.35)+generation)/2.8 + batching overhead ~ 1,420*(0.65)/2.8 ≈ 330 tokens -> 330 * 0.00095 ≈ $0.31/request.
3) Aggressive cache (50%) + batch=6 quantized model (efficiency 6x): effective compute tokens ≈ ~140 -> $0.13/request.

Recommendations for MAP gates we should surface in the doc:
- Provide a short 'cost ladder' with three scenarios (conservative, base, optimistic) with clear assumptions for cache hit, batching target, model variant.
- Include an acceptance test that runs a 30-minute soak at 1.5x peak with batching configured to expected production values. Capture tokens/request, endpoint latency, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Set a procurement-aware target: if procurement wants < $0.40/request, use the base scenario (35% cache + batch=4) as our verification target.

I attached map-gating-checklist.pdf (stub) with the gate language. If Olga approves, I'll add the exact commands we use for the soak test (k6 script + load pattern) to the shared Drive.
